stem.text: Selected values of a function f are given in the table. The function f is not defined at \( x = 5 \). What does the table suggest about \( \lim_{x \to 5} f(x) \)?

answer_key.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs approach different values on the two sides of x = 5.

worked_solution.text: From the left, the outputs 5.2000, 5.0200, 5.0020, 5.0002 approach 5.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: From the right, the outputs -2.2000, -2.0200, -2.0020, -2.0002 approach -2.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: The two sides approach different values, so the table suggests the two sided limit does not exist.
worked_solution.rule_named: two sided limit exists only when the one sided limits agree

options.label: The table suggests that the limit is 5, because the outputs approach 5 from the left of x = 5.
options.derivation: the value the left hand rows approach reported as the two sided limit

options.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because no limit can exist where f is not defined, as at x = 5.
options.derivation: nonexistence concluded from f being undefined at the target rather than from the outputs

options.label: The table suggests that the limit is -2, because the outputs approach -2 from the right of x = 5.
options.derivation: the value the right hand rows approach reported as the two sided limit
